newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: ICE HOCKEY-CZECH NATIONAL COACH BUKAC RESIGNS.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-CZECH NATIONAL COACH BUKAC RESIGNS.

text.p: Czech national ice hockey team coach Ludek Bukac said on Friday he was quitting following a widening rift between himself and several key players.

Since becoming coach in 1994 Bukac has driven out many top players, but also guided the Czechs last year to their first world championship since the former Czechoslovakia won the last of its six titles in 1985.

In recent weeks he has come under intense criticism from media and players such as NHL leading goalscorer Jaromir Jagr and top Czech Extraliga goaltender Roman Cechmanek who have said they would never again play for Bukac, branding him arrogant, incompetent and dishonest.
"For me there was no alternative," Bukac told a news conference. "I can take strong criticism but I will not let people continuously attack me."
The loss of Bukac comes at a critical time for the Czechs as they prepare to defend their world title in Helsinki.

Since winning in Vienna, last year's champions have come out on top in only three of the 18 games they have played, including an embarrassing 7-1 World Cup defeat by Germany. "I don't want to believe it but unfortunately there's nothing more I can do," said Karel Gut, chariman of the Czech Ice Hockey federation.
Bukac's assistant Zdenek Uher will take over in the interim.
After the national team's pitiful performance at last month's Sweden Cup where they finished last, losing three out of four games, veteran Drahomir Kadlec said he was humiliated by the experience.

The 31-year-old defenceman, who was a second team all-star at last year's world championships, complained that Bukac gave the players almost no instruction on the ice in Sweden and then shirked responsibility for the team's poor performance.
"No one told us what to do during the games," he said, "and when we lost the coaches didn't accept any responsibility. They looked for excuses."
At the end of the Swedish tournament, Bukac said his players had not been prepared mentally or physically and he criticised their performance at both ends of the ice.
